attacksRun.attack: CLAUDE-G18LJ-V2-SF1 is not landed (records only restate the class name / cite no exactByteIntent)
attacksRun.evidence: The gating test, and both limbs of my original finding are answered. Limb 2 charged that the v1 corpus's per-state keys were exactly {id, memberVerbatim, fixtureBytes, assertsNamedNotAuthored} with no stateNamed and no source. v2's per-state keys are {id, classMemberVerbatim, stateNamed, source, fixtureBytes, assertsNamedNotAuthored}: all 40 entries carry stateNamed AND source, and all 40 stateNamed values are distinct. Limb 1 charged that 'exactByteIntent' occurred zero times in the v1 corpus. In v2 every one of the 40 source fields cites a live exactByteIntent path, and all 40 resolve to real live class keys — crash-injection 32, conflicting-project-locks 4, process-death 4, each of which exists in live G18 v2's namedCorpusClasses. This is repair route 2 of the two the finding offered, delivered in the g16-input-corpus.v2 shape the finding named.

Live class[0] reserves the mechanism explicitly: 'It does not choose an on-disk journal format, lock-file grammar, lease API, solver, filesystem layout, or reviewed-equivalent of atomic rename.' The subject introduces none of them. 'journal format' occurs 35 times and I read every context: 32 are the artifact's own appended disclaimer 'This catalog does not choose an on-disk journal format.' on the crash states, and 3 are top-level negations (authorityClaim, whatIsNotAuthored[1], doesNot[3]). whatIsNotAuthored additionally declines a lock-file grammar, lease API, solver, filesystem layout, a reviewed-equivalent of atomic rename, and a D9/loss code. 'fcntl', 'sqlite', 'lockSchema' and 'purge' occur 0 times each. No record layout, write ordering, file name, or grammar is described anywhere.

All 40 initialStates carry fixtureBytes == 'NOT-AUTHORED' and whatIsNotAuthored[0] is 'fixture bytes'. The states name injection sites, platforms and scenarios; no byte, path, digest, record layout, or file content appears. The only bare integers in the entire 37KB file are 2 (version) and 26 (required-now).

'SATISFIED' occurs 0 times and 'QUALIFIED' 0 times. Both 'SATISFY' occurrences are negations of DR-107. status CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, reviewStatus AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW, sealRecommendation DO-NOT-SEAL, binds NOTHING. doesNot[1] additionally declines to import DR-107's PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW standing.

attacksRun.attack: the appended own-voice sentences are misattributed as live quotations (my own attack)
attacksRun.evidence: Each source reads '<live path>: <verbatim excerpt>.' followed by a sentence beginning 'This catalog' or 'This class', with no closing quotation marker, so a reader could take the trailing sentence as part of the quoted text. I decline to charge it: the pronoun shift into the artifact's own voice is itself the tell that it is a disclaimer rather than a quote, and every one of the three distinct appended sentences is supported by live — 'does not choose an on-disk journal format' and the whole G21/G09/G12 exclusion sentence appear verbatim in live class[0] and class[2] respectively as 'It ...' forms. Nothing is attributed to the harness that the harness does not say. Recorded so a successor marks the quotation boundary.

attacksRun.attack: the locks disclaimer drops a live exclusion (my own attack)
attacksRun.evidence: Live class[1] excludes three things — 'a same-project concurrent-analyze class, a live-lease activation class, or a two-cache-writer class' — while the four locks states carry only the first two. I decline to charge it: declining fewer things than live declines invents nothing and nowhere asserts the omitted class is permitted; both retained clauses are verbatim in live; and the governing exclusion remains in the pinned harness. Recorded so a fixture-authoring cycle carries the two-cache-writer exclusion forward.

observationsNotFindings: Each source appends a sentence in the artifact's own voice after a colon-introduced quotation with no closing marker, so the boundary between quoted and authored text is implicit. All three distinct appended sentences are supported by live, but a successor should mark the boundary.
The four locks states carry two of live class[1]'s three exclusions, omitting 'a two-cache-writer class'. Nothing false is asserted; a fixture-authoring cycle should carry it forward.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: ACCEPT. 16 attacks run, 14 refuted, 2 not sustained as a finding. 0 blockers, 0 MUST-FIX, 0 SHOULD-FIX. CLAUDE-G18LJ-V2-SF1 IS LANDED on its corpus limb, and both limbs of my original finding are answered: v1's per-state keys lacked stateNamed and source and 'exactByteIntent' occurred zero times in it, whereas v2 carries 40 entries each with stateNamed and source, all 40 sources citing a live exactByteIntent path that resolves to a real class key. Crucially the quoted excerpts are verbatim: my first parse reported 40 non-verbatim because it swallowed the artifact's own appended disclaimer into the quotation, and separating the own-voice sentences shows 40/40 verbatim against their own class's live intent. Coverage is 8 crash sites x 4 D-002 platforms plus 4 and 4, partitioned exactly 10 per platform with no Windows. The failure mode I watched for — satisfying the shape while inventing the reserved mechanism — did not occur: no journal format, lock-file grammar, lease API, solver, filesystem layout, fcntl, sqlite, lockSchema, D9/loss code or purge appears, and the only bare integers in 37KB are 2 and 26. The artifact carries no obligations array, so it re-measures nothing; findingDisposition scopes itself correctly to the corpus. All cited digests clean; HEAD 5d5d778; required-now 26. Two observations: the quotation boundary is implicit, and the locks states carry two of live's three exclusions.
